key.explanation: Read at equal age, retention has fallen from 47% to 28% across four consecutive cohorts. The aggregate is flat only because the newest and weakest cohorts are also the largest, which is exactly what a blended figure conceals.

Nineteen of thirty never reached first value, and seven were lost with a single relationship. Both are addressable, and both are larger than price — a discount would spend money on the cause behind four departures.
The course builds from evidence of demand into trustworthy learning, system diagnosis, customer value, economics, and finally an operating cadence.
A smoke test is a fake door: the product is not yet behind it, but the measured click or signup is a behavioural demand signal.
The result belongs to the iterate band. Rewriting the threshold or metric after the result destroys the protection the rule created.
Channel-market fit asks whether a channel's targeting, control, input, output, time, and economics match the product and ICP.
Repeated unplanned peeking and stopping on a favourable result increases the chance of declaring a fake effect.
The operating layer must preserve the evidence accumulated from validation, activation, retention, and economics. Constraint-led prioritisation connects them.
The reward acquired users temporarily. Existing-user value did not rise with network participation, so there is no demonstrated network effect.
Early LTV is an assumption-bearing estimate, not prophecy. It completes the unit-economics comparison and should be updated as cohorts mature.
Each drop applies to the remaining users, so multiple modest frictions can destroy total activation. Remove or defer nonessential pre-value work.
Growth leaks at transitions when teams optimize locally. Shared definitions and SLAs make the marketing→sales→success chain operable.
ICE is disciplined only when its three judgments are explicit and anchored to the constraint and available evidence.

Most products fail because nobody checked whether anyone wanted the thing before the building started. Lean validation answers that one question as quickly and cheaply as possible: seven to fourteen days and a few thousand rupees, against six to eighteen months and lakhs.
The split protects the proven engine while reserving capacity for adjacent and exploratory learning. Evidence can justify later reallocation.
Acquisition and conversion are not the binding constraint. The system loses accounts after purchase; more meetings accelerate the leak.

Evidence is only as strong as the cost of producing it. Praise, likes and email opens cost nothing; a signup costs a little attention; a letter of intent costs reputation; a payment — even a partial, refundable one — costs money, and money is the hardest commitment to fake.
An aha moment must be observable or defensibly proxied. Vague feelings, interest, purchase, and signup are not automatically value-realisation events.
Cohort-by-age views compare like with like and reveal whether new groups hold value better or worse.
Respondents may be sincere and still mispredict their future behaviour. Surveys are useful tools, but hypothetical willingness is weak purchase evidence.

Referral mechanics include content, product, social-proof and incentivised routes; the first choice is the mechanism the product already produces naturally, not automatically paying every customer to invite someone.

The growth operating system joins ICE, backlog, decision rules, real metrics, resource allocation and the roadmap across AARRR, and its master loop makes the output of one stage the input of the next cycle.

Test modes follow the stakes: an expensive wrong decision needs a valid test run to its sample, while a low-stakes choice may use a directional test that is reported as suggestive rather than conclusive.
MVP validation under low resources combines behavioural interest, a costly commitment and a repeatable route to the same customer before building the minimum version that performs the core job.

rubric.label: Governing ideas
rubric.description: Distinguishes demand for the product from demand for a discount, reads retention and payback by cohort rather than on blended contribution, identifies the absence of any tier above the single plan as the structural gap, and scores the backlog on evidence and effort rather than on preference.

rubric.label: Use of the numbers
rubric.description: Cites specific figures — 58% versus 21% month-three cancellation, 4% accepting the renewal price, ₹430 against ₹180 monthly contribution, ₹1,900 acquisition cost, or 340 emailed requests against nine weeks for an unrequested redesign.

rubric.label: How the ideas connect
rubric.description: Connects them: the discount bought people whose willingness to pay was never tested, so they leave before repaying a ₹1,900 acquisition cost, and permanence would convert a temporary distortion into the business's whole economics.

rubric.label: The decision
rubric.description: States that the discount should not be made permanent, names the twin-bag tier as the strongest of the three by evidence and effort, and defers the packaging redesign.

rubric.label: What would change it
rubric.description: Names what would justify a standing discount — a discounted cohort repaying acquisition cost, or the tier lifting average contribution — or states the short-term signup fall that ending it will cause.

key.explanation: The discount that paid for itself

rubric.label: Governing ideas
rubric.description: Computes or recognises net revenue retention on the existing base, reads retention by cohort at equal age rather than in aggregate, identifies the flat single plan as a structure that permits no expansion, and locates the churn cause in the leaver evidence rather than assuming it.

rubric.label: Use of the numbers
rubric.description: Cites specific figures — ₹47 lakh remaining of ₹62 lakh, or roughly 76% NRR, the cohort fall from 44% to 29%, acquisition cost from ₹3,100 to ₹5,800, the 38% reaching eight classes, or the leaver reason.

rubric.label: How the ideas connect
rubric.description: Connects them rather than listing: headline growth is new joiners masking a shrinking base, the flat plan means no retained member can add revenue, and 88% capacity is the cause of the churn rather than evidence of demand.

rubric.label: The decision
rubric.description: States that the expansion should be held or re-scoped, that the pricing structure needs a tier or commitment option, and that capacity at the times members actually attend should be fixed first.

rubric.label: What would change it
rubric.description: Names what would make the two new studios defensible — NRR above 100%, cohort curves flattening, first-month attendance rising — or states the cost and competitive risk of delaying.

key.explanation: Full classes, shrinking base
